item.title: Yamal breaks Mbappe’s record as UCL’s highest-scoring teenager [See top 5]
item.description: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has surpassed Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé to become the highest-scoring teenager in UEFA Champions League history. The 19-year-old set the new record after scoring in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa on Tuesday. Yamal capitalised on a defensive error by Villa in the seventh minute at Spotify Camp Nou, curling the ball beyond goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to register his 14th Champions League goal. The goal moved him past Mbappé, who previously held the teenage scoring record with 13 goals in the competition. Although the France international has scored 72 Champions League goals overall, Yamal has now claimed the record after just 37 appearances in Europe’s premier club competition. The Spain international has also established several other milestones in the tournament, including becoming the youngest player to start a Champions League match proper. Yamal achieved that feat at the age of 16 years and 83 days when he made his full European debut against FC Porto. His latest achievement comes after an impressive showing at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards, where he finished third behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Mbappé. The Barcelona youngster has also enjoyed a productive start to the new season, recording 13 goals and 11 assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. Top 5 Highest-Scoring Teenagers in UEFA Champions League History Lamine Yamal – 14 goals Kylian Mbappe – 13 goals Erling Haaland – 10 goals Patrick Kluivert – 7 goals Raul, Benzema and Belllingham – 6 goals each Vanguard News The post Yamal breaks Mbappe’s record as UCL’s highest-scoring teenager [See top 5] appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG Secured 2,512 Terrorism Convictions In Nine Years — NSA
item.description: Following the conclusion of the 11th phase of terrorism trials at the Federal High Court, Abuja, the federal government said it has secured a total of 2,512 convictions in terrorism-related cases over nine years. National Coordinator of the National Counter Terrorism Centre, Office of the National Security Adviser, Major General Adamu Laka, disclosed this during a press briefing in Abuja on Tuesday. According to him, the latest phase, conducted in October 2026, recorded 791 additional convictions out of 1,069 cases handled across 10 courts. He said the trials demonstrated the government’s commitment to combating terrorism, holding perpetrators and their financiers accountable, and strengthening the administration of justice while upholding the rule of law and the fundamental rights of defendants. The National Coordinator said the judgment showed the seriousness with which Nigeria’s justice system addresses terrorism and affirms that perpetrators, regardless of affiliation, were accountable under the law when criminal responsibility was established beyond reasonable doubt. Major General Laka revealed that among the significant outcomes of this phase was the conviction and sentencing to death of Suleiman Abu, in the case of the Federal Republic of Nigeria versus Suleiman Abu. He said the Federal High Court found him guilty of Boko Haram membership and participation in terrorist attacks on military facilities and civilians, resulting in deaths and serious injuries. He said, “I am therefore pleased to report that the 11th phase of terrorism trials recorded significant outcomes. Prior to this phase, the first 10 phases had resulted in a cumulative total of 1,721 convictions. “During the 11th phase, an additional 791 convictions were recorded, bringing the cumulative number of convictions across all 11 phases to 2,512 convictions. “In this last phase, a total of 1,069 cases were handled across 10 courts of the Federal High Court sitting in Abuja. “The outcomes are as follows: 791 convictions; seven acquittals; 41 discharges; four cases struck out; three cases withdrawn; 211 cases adjourned; 11 cases pending; and one case recorded under another category.” According to him, the judgment showed the seriousness with which Nigeria’s justice system addresses terrorism and affirms that perpetrators, regardless of affiliation, were accountable under the law when criminal responsibility was established beyond reasonable doubt. item.title: Fernandes critical of media 'lies' about Carrick relationship
item.description: Bruno Fernandes' penalty sparked Manchester United's second-half revival against Roma [Getty Images] Bruno Fernandes says "a lot of lies" have been reported about his relationship with Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick in recent weeks. Speaking after United's 3-2 win over Roma on Tuesday, it was the first time the 32-year-old had addressed the media since being dropped to the bench after publicly criticising Carrick's tactics in the wake of their 4-1 loss at Como. Restored to the team for the Premier League defeat by Chelsea, captain Fernandes converted a 58th-minute penalty against Roma to spark an improbable second-half comeback from 2-0 down. "It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media," Fernandes told Amazon Prime. "A lot of lies around many things that have happened between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air , then after that the manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I'm not performing. That's fair. "Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. And, if it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. "It doesn't change the belief I have of the manager and the staff and every player in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me." Victory against Roma ended a run of nine games without a win, easing some of the pressure on Carrick after a challenging period. But when asked if the result would save his job, Fernandes told Amazon Prime: "We don't need to save anyone's job." He added: "The club needed that win, the players needed that win. We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together." Former Leicester goalkeeper Kasper Schmeichel said on BBC Radio 5 Live he liked Fernandes' comments and that he hoped "they can draw a line under all this public stuff and they can get back to winning games". "In Bruno Fernandes' defence is that I've been in football a long time and what's reported in the media is a fraction of the truth usually," said Schmeichel. "The amount of times I saw something written about the clubs I was playing in that couldn't be further from the truth was absolutely staggering. "I hope for Manchester United and Michael Carrick they can draw a line under all this public stuff and they can get back to winning games like they did today." Man Utd produce incredible second-half comeback to beat Roma Man Utd beat Roma - the other great Champions League comebacks 'That's how we repay Carrick' After winning 12 of his 17 games in charge last season to guide United back into the Champions League after a two-year absence, Carrick was given a two-year contract. However, things have quickly unravelled this season and United sit 17th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening nine games. item.title: A half-time speech, a retaken penalty - and a win to save Carrick's job?
item.description: [Getty Images] We cannot know how important Bryan Cristante's foot touching the Roma penalty area as Bruno Fernandes took his initial spot-kick at Old Trafford will prove to be for Michael Carrick. In the moment, as the Roma fans celebrated, and Manchester United trailed 2-0, it seemed catastrophic for the club and terminal for Carrick's position as head coach. But the video assistant referee (VAR) Carlos del Cerro Grande stepped in, advised a retake was required - and at the very least changed the course of the night. Fernandes kept his nerve to drive home his second attempt and then, in a frenzied atmosphere, Matheus Cunha scored twice in the final seven minutes. Even without the context of everything that came before the game, it was the most improbable of comebacks. Even Cunha's sending off soon after, which ensured a nervy ending, would not deny United a first win in 10, bringing some respite after a dreadful few weeks. How did Carrick feel when the penalty was saved? And what did he say at half-time in response to a desperate first-half display that brought condemnation from legendary United figures Wayne Rooney and Nicky Butt, who were covering the game for Amazon Prime? In that moment, there was even a sense of deja vu. "I knew at half-time against Watford," recalled Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in September 2023 of his own dismissal as United boss a couple of years earlier. "At half-time, I told the players it was probably going to be the last time we worked together." United were two goals down at Vicarage Road at half-time that day. Carrick was on the bench as one of Solskjaer's coaches. They went on to lose 4-1. Not this time. We don't need to save anyone's job, says Man Utd captain Fernandes Man Utd beat Roma - the other great Champions League comebacks Man Utd produce incredible second-half comeback to beat Roma Despite the bleakness of the situation, Carrick clearly has a more positive mindset. "At half-time, I was wanting them to be more positive if anything, and not get too disappointed and frustrated," said Carrick. "The easiest thing is when you keep trying to do something is feeling sorry for yourself. If something goes wrong, you get disappointed. That's not going to help anybody. We might as well all go home if that's the case. We've got to keep looking for the next moment, the next solution. "I don't like to keep talking to the lads about what this place can do and the history and what's gone before too much, but it's there. "This place does magical things, it's done it before and it'll do it over and over again at some point in the future. There's just something in this place that when we do have these types of nights, we do it the hard way. "But one moment can flip the whole place in a different direction. I spoke about that with the boys. Let's have one moment that can trigger it. And we had that." item.title: Emery takes positives, but Villa 'have work to do' to reach Barca level
item.description: Barcelona have won 13 of their 15 games this season after beating Aston Villa [Getty Images] Unai Emery punched the air in frustration at the Spotify Nou Camp. It came from a place of disappointment and exasperation as his Aston Villa side let slip the opportunity of a result in their Champions League tie against Barcelona. They had just fallen 2-0 behind in Spain, having tried to match the hosts blow-for-blow. Raphinha's quick second-half double put the game out of reach after Lamine Yamal's opener, when Villa pressed the self-destruct button just seven minutes in. It could have led to a collapse but, instead, they took the game to the Spanish champions during an engrossing first half, which could - and perhaps should - have yielded a leveller. While defeat ended their 100% Champions League start after three wins, it gave Villa and boss Emery the chance to consider their progress. Barcelona brilliance ends Villa's perfect start Villa firmly believe they belong on this stage. After four years of improvement with Emery they have another chance to prove it. They arrived in Spain with wins against Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, but this was their hardest test. Emery, who celebrated his 55th birthday on Tuesday, wanted to use it as a barometer for their progress, to see how they compared with the current La Liga leaders and five-time European champions. In the driving rain Villa could argue they matched Barca in the opening period and had it not been for Joao Gomes' glaring error that led to Lamine Yamal's strike, and poor finishing, they could have snatched the advantage. Yet they fell short. They have been on the rise under Emery but last season's Europa League winners showed they are still not at the level to win in the Nou Camp. The head coach would also deny it, but perhaps he had something to prove in this stadium which handed him his harshest lesson in the competition nine years ago. In what became known as La Remontada [The Comeback], Barcelona recovered from 4-0 down from the first leg of their last-16 tie to beat Emery's Paris St-Germain side 6-1 in the home return and 6-5 on aggregate. "One more match. Just one more match," said Emery when asked about it on Monday. There was to be no Villa comeback on Tuesday night and Emery's record at the Nou Camp now stands at 15 defeats in 16 games and, in 31 attempts against Barca, he had won just three times. He was able to field what was his strongest available team, but they created their own problems when Gomes' wretched pass gifted Lamine Yamal the crucial opener. Emery, whose side were overtaken by second-placed Barcelona in the league phase table, added: "We are working for years together and we made mistakes like that but we have always overcome those mistakes. I am not blaming him." The self-inflicted wound, though, failed to discourage Villa as they refused to lie down and accept a Barcelona victory. item.title: 'I didn't feel relief!' - Michael Carrick refuses to get carried away as Man Utdend winless run with dramatic Roma comeback
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-MAN UTD-ROMA - AFP Michael Carrick has described Manchester United’s dramatic comeback victory over Roma as an "important night" for the club, though he was quick to downplay suggestions that their season has reached a definitive turning point. The Red Devils overcame a two-goal deficit at Old Trafford to secure a vital 3-2 win, halting a dismal run of ten matches without a victory. Old Trafford witnesses a thriller Manchester United found themselves trailing by two goals against Roma inside 17 minutes on Tuesday evening. The hosts looked destined for another disappointing result before mounting a stunning response to claim a 3-2 victory . The result halted a miserable sequence of three consecutive defeats for the Premier League side. More importantly, it marked their first triumph across their last nine fixtures, injecting some much-needed positivity into a turbulent campaign. Pride takes precedence over relief Despite the immense pressure surrounding his position, Carrick insisted the full-time whistle did not bring him a sense of personal salvation. Instead, the 45-year-old manager focused purely on his squad's resilience and character in overturning the deficit. "Genuinely, no," Carrick responded when asked if he felt relieved. "Whether that's right or wrong, or normal or not, I don't know, but I didn't feel relief. I was genuinely pleased for the players." He praised the effort required to secure the victory, highlighting the determination shown on the pitch. "I could feel their willingness to do well, and so for them to have to dig really deep, and just for everybody, you know," he added. Responsibility and staying grounded The Manchester United boss acknowledged the weight of expectations at Old Trafford, noting how crucial the victory was for collective morale. "I feel the responsibility of that, so to see everybody having that feeling that we all crave. That's why we're all here," Carrick explained. "I really 100 per cent wasn't thinking about myself at that moment - it was just more seeing everybody and the feeling that we can generate when we do things right." While visibly proud of the comeback, Carrick immediately tempered expectations. He refused to label the win a definitive turning point for the club. "I'm not getting too carried away with things," he stated. "I think it's an important night. But we've got to take stock, we've got to stay calm and prepare and be ready for another big game on the weekend." Premier League survival battle United must now attempt to translate this momentum into domestic stability as they return to Premier League action to face Aston Villa before the November international break. Carrick's men currently languish in 17th place in the table , sitting above the relegation zone strictly on goal difference. Securing a positive result against Villa this weekend is essential if the Red Devils are to climb away from the bottom three and begin salvaging their league campaign.

item.title: Gardner-Johnson released by Bills after spitting ban
item.description: CJ Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the game against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter [Getty Images] The Buffalo Bills have released safety CJ Gardner-Johnson after he served a one-game suspension for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders' Brock Bowers. The 28-year-old, whose appeal against the decision was rejected, missed week eight's 36-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens. NFL Network reported on Tuesday that the Bills' decision was driven more by inconsistency in Gardner-Johnson's performances than by the spitting incident. Gardner-Johnson started the first six games after joining the team during the off-season. He recorded 26 tackles, two passes defended and one interception for the Bills. Damar Hamlin replaced him in the starting line-up against the Ravens and is likely to retain his place in the team. Gardner-Johnson has also played for the Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions, Houston Texans, Baltimore Ravens and Chicago Bears since leaving the New Orleans Saints at the end of the 2021 season. A fourth-round pick by the New Orleans Saints in 2019, Gardner-Johnson helped the Eagles win the Super Bowl in 2024. NFL fixtures and results Get American Football news sent straight to your phone

item.title: Red Sox’s perfect trade offer for Reds’ Elly De La Cruz
item.description: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images. Red Sox’s perfect trade offer for Reds’ Elly De La Cruz appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox should pursue Elly De La Cruz with an offer substantial enough to give the Cincinnati Reds a difficult decision. Franklin Arias, Payton Tolle, and Justin Gonzales would provide a potential shortstop successor, an established young starter, and another promising bat. The Athletic’s Jim Bowden identified De La Cruz as a potential target in his assessment of Boston’s offseason plans. “The Red Sox will also continue to call the Nationals regarding a possible CJ Abrams trade and the Reds if Cincinnati decides to move Elly De La Cruz. Either way, expect them to be aggressive with the aim of adding at least a bat or two.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The assessment does not establish the Reds intend to trade their star. The following package is an editorial proposal, not a reported offer or an established asking price. Hypothetical trade Red Sox receive Elly De La Cruz Reds receive Franklin Arias, Payton Tolle and Justin Gonzales Why Elly De La Cruz fits Boston’s future The Red Sox scored 689 runs in 2026, ranking 23rd in the majors. De La Cruz would address that weakness after hitting .283 with a .365 on-base percentage, .515 slugging percentage, 30 home runs and 30 stolen bases. At 24, the switch-hitter offers more than an immediate boost. His remaining control through 2029 would give Boston three seasons to build around him before free agency, making a substantial investment more defensible than surrendering premium talent for a rental. The clearest defensive plan would put De La Cruz at shortstop and explore moving Trevor Story to second base. Story’s previous experience there makes that a practical option, although Boston would need to evaluate how the change affects its other infield options. Story’s contract runs through 2027 with a club option for 2028. Acquiring De La Cruz would address Boston’s longer-term shortstop outlook while immediately strengthening the lineup. The Red Sox would be paying for established production during a player’s prime. However, Arias could become an excellent major league shortstop himself. Trading him would mean choosing De La Cruz’s demonstrated ability over the possibility of developing a less expensive alternative. Why the Reds should consider this return The Reds finished the 2026 season 75-87 and last in the National League Central. That record creates reason to reconsider the roster’s construction, but it does not make trading De La Cruz necessary. Arias supplies the potential successor . The 20-year-old ranks second overall on MLB Pipeline’s prospect list after batting .323/.400/.557 with 25 home runs between Double-A and Triple-A in 2026. item.title: Angel Reese announces return to LSU for exciting appearance after losing the WNBA Finals
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Atlanta Dream’s Angel Reese is preparing for her first major public appearance since losing Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals, returning to her alma mater. Reese finally delivered on the potential her ardent supporters have said she has in the 2026 WNBA season, leading the Dream to the WNBA Finals in her first season with the team, but losing Game 7 and the title to the Golden State Valkyries. Despite the loss, Reese has cemented her status as one of the best players in the WNBA as the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and the star of a Finals team. Her upcoming plans also highlight her confident attitude. LSU Tigers plan halftime recognition for Angel Reese after WNBA Finals Despite the loss, LSU has announced a halftime recognition ceremony for Reese during their November 5 clash against the Texas Southern Tigers at the Pete Maravich Assembly Center. Reese announced the same on her personal channels with a fitting caption. “The Bayou Barbie is back.” The Tigers will honour Reese after an incredible season in the professional world as a DPOY winner and leading the Dream to the Finals despite not being pre-season favourites. Reese averaged 16.4 points, 12.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals in the regular season and 16.1 points, 11.0 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.7 blocks in the playoffs. Reese won one national championship during her two seasons with the Tigers, famously beating Caitlin Clark’s Iowa Hawkeyes 102-85 in the 2023 NCAA Division I Women’s Tournament Final. This was LSU’s first national championship in Division I women’s basketball. While we have seen certain athletes go away from the media for a while after losing a championship game, Reese is showing that she is willing to bask in the well-deserved appreciation she will get after a career-defining season. As long as the 24-year-old forward is motivated to come back next season and achieve even more, events like this will be frequent at LSU, especially with the shared strong bond between the program and the player. item.description: US President Donald Trump said rival Democrats had done "a good job" Tuesday after they gained control of Congress in the midterm elections. While Trump acknowledged that the Iran war may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party, he did not take personal responsability for the result that will upend the last two years of his presidency.

item.title: Retiring Serrano wants to end as a 'game-changer'
item.description: WBO and WBA featherweight champion Amanda Serrano will fight at Coliseo de Puerto Rico for the first time when she faces Skye Falzon [Getty Images] Amanda Serrano said she wants to be remembered as a "game-changer" as she prepares for her farewell fight on home soil next year. Puerto Rico's seven-division world champion will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight titles against Australia's Skye Falzon in San Juan on 9 January. Serrano, who holds a 50-4-1 record with 32 knockouts, previously announced she will retire after the bout , which has been dubbed "The Last Walk" by promoters. "I want people to remember me as a game-changer," Serrano said at a news conference. "I gave it my all in the ring. Every time I fought, every time I trained, I just left everything in the ring, and I hope that you guys see that." Serrano is chasing the women's knockout record, which she jointly shares with American Christy Martin. While Serrano suggested the record would be the "cherry on top", she also wants to make the most of her final appearance in the ring. "I made sure that I went back to the 12 three-minute rounds because I want to enjoy every second, every minute of my last fight in there," the 38-year-old said. "I'm going to go out there and give it my all. If the knockout comes, it comes." Serrano to end career in Puerto Rico in January Serrano draws 3.4m views on TikTok for 50th win Serrano equals knockout record with Hanson victory Falzon, also 38, who holds a 12-2 record with seven knockouts, said it was a dream come true to get the chance to fight Serrano. "I actually cried about it," said Falzon. "The opportunity is something I'm going to grab hold of and I just can't wait. "I'm not here just to take part in Amanda's history, I'm here to try to write my own. I wouldn't be a fighter if I didn't believe I could win." Serrano welcomed the confidence from the Australian, saying: "I wouldn't like if any of my opponents would come thinking they're going to come to lose. I love to fight the best out there." Serrano is the first and only Puerto Rican boxer, male or female, to become undisputed world champion, and in 2022 she and Ireland's Katie Taylor became the first female boxers to headline New York's Madison Square Garden. She also defeated Brazil's Danila Ramos in 2023 in the first-ever women's unified world championship contested over 12 three-minute rounds, which is equal to a men's championship fight. Serrano said her decision to retire was simply down to time and she always knew she would hang up her gloves in Puerto Rico. "You guys [have] been with me from the very beginning, supporting me, loving me, and I've been fighting for you guys," added Serrano, who was born in Carolina on the island. "I bring my flag with me, it's in my heart. I'm always with you, and I fight for you. I just want you guys to celebrate my long journey, and it's going to be a great night." item.title: Soludo seeks pharmacists’ support against fake drugs
item.description: By Steve Oko Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for stronger collaboration with the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to tackle fake drugs, improve healthcare delivery and position the state as a major pharmaceutical hub. Soludo made the call while declaring open the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged Ijele 2026, in Awka. Speaking on the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact,” the governor described pharmacists as indispensable partners in building an efficient and sustainable healthcare system. He urged the professional body to work with his administration to enforce standards and sanitise the pharmaceutical sector, particularly by tackling counterfeit medicines and illegal operators posing as licensed pharmacies. Soludo said his administration was consolidating Anambra’s position as a pharmaceutical hub through the development of a pharmaceutical hub in Oba and a Coordinated Wholesale Centre, which he said was expected to be completed early next year. The governor also highlighted his administration’s investments in education and healthcare, saying the provision of free education from kindergarten to secondary school had reduced the state’s out-of-school children rate to 0.25 per cent, which he described as the lowest in the country. He further disclosed that the state had strengthened its primary healthcare system, provided free antenatal services to more than 250,000 beneficiaries and conducted over 950 free caesarean operations for expectant mothers. Earlier, PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, commended Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession. Ibrahim described Anambra’s hosting of the conference as the fulfilment of a longstanding commitment and praised the governor’s leadership and vision. He said the conference provided an opportunity to deepen cooperation between the pharmaceutical profession and government towards improving healthcare delivery. The post Soludo seeks pharmacists’ support against fake drugs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Manchester United co-owners INEOS sack manager after just five months in charge amid growing pressure on Michael Carrick
item.description: Sir Jim Ratcliffe Manchester United 2024 HIC - Getty Images Manchester United minority owners INEOS have sanctioned a managerial dismissal at FC Lausanne-Sport while debate intensifies over the future of Old Trafford boss Michael Carrick. Sir Jim Ratcliffe's chemical group parted ways with head coach Luka Elsner on Tuesday after just five months in charge of the struggling Swiss outfit. Swiss club dismiss head coach Lausanne-Sport confirmed the exit of 44-year-old tactician Elsner on Tuesday after a dismal start left them rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League table. Appointed on June 1, the manager suffered eight losses across his opening 12 league fixtures while also overseeing two domestic cup ties. His departure arrives shortly after Ratcliffe placed both Lausanne and French club Nice up for sale to streamline his sporting portfolio. Official statement confirms mutual exit Announcing the managerial change via an official club release, Lausanne-Sport stated: "After extensive discussions regarding the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration. "Having taken over as Lausanne's manager on June 1st, Luka Elsner led the first team in 12 Brack Super League matches and two rounds of the Swiss Cup. FC Lausanne-Sport wishes to emphasise the professionalism and commitment that Luka Elsner has demonstrated since his arrival. "He dedicated himself to the club's project with high standards, expertise, and a constant desire to develop his team. His methodological approach and tools also contributed to the development of the coaching staff. "These contributions have enriched the club, which will continue to build upon these achievements. Given that results remain crucial in professional football, the current sporting dynamics have led all parties to agree that ending their collaboration is now the best decision for FC Lausanne-Sport." Old Trafford protests target owners With INEOS scaling back their multi-club operations elsewhere in Europe, the British billionaire's primary footballing focus remains firmly on United, where Carrick's position is under threat following persistent inconsistency that has left them languishing in 17th place in the Premier League. However, supporters are also directing fierce anger at Ratcliffe and the Glazer family as the board weigh up a dugout change. During Tuesday night's Champions League home fixture against Roma, fans in the Stretford End halted play in the 21st minute by throwing green and gold balloons onto the turf while chanting against the owners. At that point, the hosts already trailed 2-0 and were subsequently jeered off at the interval. European comeback eases elimination fears Despite the toxic atmosphere during the opening 45 minutes, United rallied after the restart to secure a 3-2 victory courtesy of a Bruno Fernandes penalty and a brace from Matheus Cunha. item.title: Inside Andrej Acimovic, Melakih Cunningham's big nights in season opener
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — It was a strong start to the season for Missouri State (1-0) men’s basketball on Tuesday, Nov. 3. The Bears dispatched Division II Lincoln 88-60. Missouri State trailed 14-11 inside the first seven minutes of the game. The Bears followed with a 32-9 run, which gave them the lead they needed for a comfortable victory. Here are some takeaways from Missouri State’s win. Andrej Acimovic shines in debut Missouri State newcomer Andrej Acimovic made his mark. The Bosnian native scored a game-high 24 points on 9-for-16 shooting. The sophomore did not feature for Indiana last season. This was the first college game of his career and the 6-foot-11 center enjoyed every second of it. “The honor is to these guys for passing me the ball,” Acimovic said. “It was just layups and shooting. My job is not hard.” The Bears dominated the paint thanks to Acimovic’s presence, outscoring Lincoln 44-20 inside the lane. Missouri State: Meet the revamped men's basketball roster Trey Williams finished with a double-double. He scored 11 points and dished out 10 assists. Williams found Acimovic early and often for easy baskets. “He’s great with his back to the basket,” Williams said. “He can really pass the ball, too. His job was to score tonight, but you will see him pass the ball a lot more too.” Melakih Cunningham drops new career-high One of three returners, Melakih Cunningham did not miss a beat. The sophomore guard came off the bench and tied for the most minutes on the floor with guard Jordan Blair and Williams. Cunningham scored a new career-high 19 points on 7-for-8 shooting. He was on fire from behind the arc, going 5-for-6 from 3-point range. “This week, I made a lot of threes in practice,” Cunningham said. “Coming to the game, I was already confident in the work that I’ve put in. It was no surprise to me.” Missouri State: Why depth can be a difference maker for women's basketball Another scoring guard will help Missouri State’s roster this season. If Cunningham can make 3-pointers consistently, he will be a dangerous player because of his athleticism in creating shots at the rim. “One of his biggest strengths is actually posting up,” head coach Cuonzo Martin said. “He’s a high-level shooter, and he spends so much time working on this game. You are always happy for a guy like that, who puts that type of work in.” Cuonzo Martin's take on opening win This is Martin's third season in his second stint with the Bears. With 12 new players, Missouri State saw a new roster hit the floor. For the majority of the first half, the team rotated eight players. Guard Dylan Rowe, forward Christian Thompson, Williams, Acimovic and Blair started in the first lineup. Cunningham was one of the first players off the bench with forward Matt Gray and forward Ngundeng Ruey. item.title: Why Brian Kelly is riding with Ole Miss vs. Georgia
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Why Brian Kelly is riding with Ole Miss vs. Georgia appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former LSU Tigers head coach Brian Kelly is doubling down on his SEC takes, and this time he’s rolling with the University of Mississippi. Ahead of another explosive clash between the Ole Miss Rebels and the University of Georgia, Kelly voiced full confidence in head coach Lane Kiffin’s squad. His reasoning is simple: The Rebels have already proven it can knock off the heavyweight Bulldogs. That bold belief stems directly from their iconic College Football Playoff Quarterfinal thriller at the Sugar Bowl, where the Rebels edged out Georgia 39-34 in a high-stakes masterpiece. Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss put on an absolute clinic, dissecting Georgia’s defense by completing 30 of 46 passes for 362 yards and two touchdowns without throwing a single interception. Tailback Kewan Lacy added muscle on the ground, taking 22 carries for 98 rushing yards and two touchdowns to keep the Bulldogs on their heels all night. Wide receiver Harrison Wallace III hauled in nine receptions for 156 yards and a score, while placekicker Lucas Carneiro drilled a clutch 47-yard field goal with six seconds remaining to seal the victory. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton tried to rally his team with 203 passing yards, one passing touchdown, and two rushing scores, but the Rebels racked up 473 total yards to outlast the Bulldogs. Caitlin Clark had averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists during the regular season to cap off a franchise-best 28 regular-season wins for Indiana. Now the Fever star has named the Aces’ A’ja Wilson as the toughest player in the WNBA to guard. Clark made the pick during Tuesday’s episode of Kylie Kelce’s “Not Gonna Lie” podcast and used the playoff series to make her case. Caitlin Clark Ties Her A’ja Wilson Pick to Indiana’s Playoff Loss Asked to name the hardest players to guard in the WNBA, Clark went with Wilson and began by discussing the matchup problems the Las Vegas superstar creates. Wilson won a record fifth MVP award this season, her third straight, while the Aces finished the regular season 31-13. “In the W, definitely A’ja. I think that would probably be everybody’s answer. Like, just so difficult. Just her size, her physicality, her athleticism,” Clark said . The Fever star then moved to the ways Wilson can score: “She can make midrange jump shots super consistently. She can stretch the floor when she wants to, and she can finish around the rim really well.” READ MORE: ‘I Love That Fandom’ — Caitlin Clark Makes Feelings Clear About ‘Passionate’ Philadelphia Fans As Kylie Kelce Floats Bold Move Clark linked her pick directly to how Indiana’s season ended, noting, “that’s who we lost to this year in the first round… When you let a player like that see the first couple baskets go in, it’s like, ‘Ah, it’s going to be a long night, like you’re going to have 30.'” Clark pointed to Game 2 in Indianapolis as the exception: “So that’s what we did well in Game 2, the game that we won, like we made it difficult on her from the start.” Wilson finished the Fever’s 99-89 win with 22 points on 5-for-11 shooting, committing 4 turnovers in 34 minutes, and 12 of her points came at the free-throw line. Clark was just as candid about the other two games, saying, “Then in Game 1 and Game 3, she kind of just had her way, and it was what it was. You know, it’s usually she’s going to get what she gets, and you kind of have to try to limit everybody else.” Wilson cleared 30 points in both of the Aces’ wins against the Fever. She had 38 points on 15-for-19 shooting with 16 rebounds and 4 blocks in a 102-85 Game 1 win, when Las Vegas led by as many as 27. In the clincher, the three-time champion poured in 36 points on 11-for-18 shooting, knocking down 12 of 15 free throws. item.title: Christian Bale opens up about playing Raiders owner Al Davis in ‘Madden’ movie
item.description: Christian Bale opens up about playing Raiders owner Al Davis in ‘Madden’ movie appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the 2026 NFL season in full swing, Las Vegas Raiders fans have an additional treat to look forward to in the form of David O. Russell’s new movie Madden , which features Christian Bale in a supporting role playing the late, great Al Davis . Stopping by SportsCenter to talk about the role with ESPN’s Kevin Negandhi, Bale broke down what it’s like to fill the shoes of such an iconic NFL figure and why Davis is much more complicated than some might think. “Yeah, I mean, the man never backed down from a fight, loved to fight. That was the story that he would say that his dad never let him back down from a fight, ever. He knew every single role within the Raiders. You know, he started as a scout, became assistant coach, coach, he’d been general manager, you know, he was a commissioner and then owner. And he wasn’t somebody with a lot of money who came in and bought the team. He earned his way up to have that team. So we understood everything about it. He was always down on the field,” Bale explained. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He had that motto, you know, once a Raider, always a Raider. And he really stood by it. You know, the man said, ‘All right, to get respect, you’ve got to be feared.’ And I think he liked people to think about him that way. But the people who loved him and knew him very well said he didn’t like to broadcast the fact that he had a really big heart and he genuinely took care of everybody who had been in his inner circle within the Raiders. No matter how many years they’ve been gone, he still took care of them. “And incredible things that he did. You know, he wouldn’t allow the team to play in cities that segregated players. And then on top of that, you know, he had this great civil rights record. He was the first owner to hire an African-American coach in Art Shell, a Latino coach in Tom Flores, and a female executive director in Amy Trask. And they wanted to actually call that the Al Davis rule. And he said, no, no, I don’t want that. Don’t give me that credit. So he was a great contradiction, as all good characters are.” Recalled fondly for his perfectly coiffed hair, need for speed, and iconic “Just win, baby” catchphrase, Davis is a big reason why the NFL is the most popular sport in the United States and continues to grow each and every year globally. While only time will tell how he performs in Russell’s picture, if his track record is of any indication, it’s safe to assume Bale will do a bang-up job stealing every scene he’s in. "He had that motto, 'Once a Raider always a Raider', and he really stood by it." Christian Bale joins SportsCenter to discuss his upcoming role as the legendary Al Davis in the film 'Madden' ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/4qxy6xAZii — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 4, 2026 Related: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions

This week, Brady addressed the emotional aspect of the occasion as he returns to the stadium where he became one of the most recognizable names on the planet. Tom Brady Addresses Emotional New England Return During an appearance on Tuesday’s segment of “The Herd” with host Colin Cowherd, Brady spoke about the Patriots organization in glowing terms and detailed how he would approach calling the game without making it about himself. “It will be certainly emotional; every inch of that stadium I’ve been through so many times, from the locker rooms to the meeting rooms, the fields,” Brady said . “Just so many memorable plays in that stadium. Big games, championship games, rivalry games, division-clinching games. So to be back there and to really understand what that Patriot organization is all about and to convey that to the fans in a way I’m not talking about myself. “I’m really talking about this awesome program that’s been built, and the Patriots always seem to do things the right way. Last year, the Super Bowl kind of came out of nowhere. Such a terrible season the year before. Coach (Mike) Vrabel comes in and really resets the entire environment.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Brady was selected No. 199 overall by the Patriots in the 2000 NFL Draft and is still the greatest draft steal of all time, given his body of work. In 20 seasons in New England, the four-time Super Bowl MVP led the Patriots to 17 division titles, nine AFC conference titles, an undefeated regular season in 2007 and six Super Bowl championships. item.title: Why rugby league needs Tonga-Samoa World Cup final
item.description: Tonga and Samoa met in front of a colourful and fervent crowd in Sydney on Sunday [Getty Images] With blow out wins and a convoluted format, the men's group stage at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup did little to dissuade cynics about the unhealthy state of the international game. From Group A, Australia and New Zealand came through as expected and are widely tipped to face off in the final on 15 November. But from the strange lands of Group B-C, two beacons of hope have emerged. Tonga will face New Zealand after winning all three group matches, before Samoa face Australia in a repeat of the 2022 final. And if either goes all the way, it would be good for international rugby league, shaking up the game in the same way Wakefield's Grand Final win has for the Super League – proving there is still room for surprises in rugby league. "Could this be a dress rehearsal for the final? I hope so," former Bradford Bulls head coach Matthew Elliott told BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra after Tonga and Samoa's riveting Group B-C match, won 20-18 by the Tongans . "I shouldn't say that out loud as an Aussie but I hope so." History suggests this scenario is unlikely, but not impossible. The first semi-final, New Zealand v Tonga, is a match with a dramatic recent history. Tonga beat New Zealand 25-14 in an epic Pacific Championships match two years ago to reach their first-ever elite tournament final. Last year, their meeting was overshadowed by a head injury to Tonga back-rower Eli Katoa, who needed emergency brain surgery after receiving three separate concussions and has not played since. Tonga were semi-finalists in 2017, winning their group after stunning New Zealand 28-22 in the group stage. In the last four they were only narrowly defeated by England, 20-18, scoring three tries in the final seven minutes to give the English a huge fright in their best previous World Cup effort. 'It was an absolute cracker' Tonga and Samoa have met 23 times - both have won 11, with one ending in a draw [Getty Images] Samoa have gone one further of course and were surprise runners-up four years ago having not previously gone beyond the quarter-finals since first appearing at the World Cup in 1995. They were beaten 60-6 by England in their opener but fought through to the semi-finals, where they stunned the hosts 27-26 in a golden point win at Emirates Stadium. At Old Trafford they were overpowered by Australia but not overawed, losing 30-10 . In doing so Samoa became only the sixth different team to reach a men's final after Australia, New Zealand, Great Britain, England and France, in 16 editions. Australia have won 10 of the last 11 World Cups, including the last three, with New Zealand winning the other. Such dominance at the supposed peak of the sport, in a tournament reduced from 16 to 10 teams this year, indicates a gap growing between haves and have nots. Of the outsiders, Samoa and Tonga can shake that up. The teams met at the quarter-final stage of the last Rugby League Worl

India batting updates After 10 overs, India are 49/1 Rohit Sharma departed in the very first over (0.6 ov) without scoring, falling for a 6-ball duck after chipping Kyle Jamieson to Mitchell Santner. Virat Kohli settled the nerves as he raced to 24* off 24 balls with 4 boundaries by the 10th over mark to keep the required run rate well in check. New Zealand batting updates After 40.2 overs, NZ are 185/10 Arshdeep Singh broke through immediately in the 32nd over (31.1 ov) to dismiss Kyle Jamieson (1 off 6). He struck again in the 36th over (35.1 ov) when Shreyas Iyer took his third catch of the innings to remove Glenn Phillips (30 off 51), leaving Arshdeep with figures of 4/70 from his full 10 overs. Anshul Kamboj completed an exceptional 10-over spell, finishing with remarkable figures of 10-2-22-2 at an economy rate of just 2.20 with 46 dot balls. Reduced to 146/9, New Zealand mounted an improbable, aggressive 39-run resistance for the 10th wicket. No. 11 Blair Tickner launched a blistering cameo, clobbering 4 sixes and a boundary on his way to 34 off 22 balls. After 30 overs, NZ are 124/7 The middle-overs slide gathered pace in the 22nd over (21.1 ov) when Daryl Mitchell was run out for 28 (41b, 3x4, 1x6), leaving the Kiwis reeling at 97/5. Kamboj bowled an exceptional, suffocating eight-over spell (8-2-14-2). He breached the defense of Kiwi skipper Mitchell Santner (4 off 16) to rattle the stumps in the 27th over (26.1 ov). Two overs later (28.3 ov), Kamboj struck again as Nathan Smith (1 off 9) offered a simple chance to Virat Kohli, plunging New Zealand to 115/7. Axar Patel slipped through four economical overs without fuss, giving away just 9

item.title: Real Madrid on verge of signing Manchester United wonderkid as Barcelona drop out of race
item.description: Real Madrid on verge of signing Manchester United wonderkid as Barcelona drop out of race Real Madrid are closing in on signing another young talent for the future, with JJ Gabriel said to be close to joining Los Blancos . The 16-year-old Englishman’s future has been in the news for a couple of months now, ever since he decided he wanted to leave Manchester United. Touted as the biggest English talent around, a number of European clubs were in the race to sign the teenager. However, according to Matteo Moretto , Los Blancos are extremely close to signing the 16-year-old attacker. Gabriel has been training in the Spanish capital for the past few days while waiting for his future to be finalised. Real Madrid closing in on JJ Gabriel Los Blancos are set to pip the likes of Barcelona, PSG and Bayern Munich, who were all interested in JJ Gabriel. The Catalan club are now said to be completely out of the race after refusing to enter an expensive bidding war for his signature. JJ Gabriel is on his way to Real Madrid. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) For a 16-year-old, Gabriel’s camp are said to be making some significant demands that not every club is willing to meet. However, Real Madrid, as always, are willing to look at what he can become rather than what he is today. Los Blancos have carefully assessed the contractual and regulatory implications of signing the youngster, given his age. Although the deal is close, it has not been officially completed, with January 2027 being the earliest possible registration window. Another major investment from Los Blancos Gabriel’s potential explains why Real Madrid have pursued him so persistently. JJ Gabriel is an exciting talent for the future. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) The versatile attacker has impressed at youth level with his dribbling, creativity and goalscoring instincts. He even scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut and has always looked at home in much older age groups. His arrival at Real Madrid would not be about making a signing for this season, but rather for the future. Signing him would only be the beginning. At 16, Real Madrid need to plan his development and handle him very carefully. For now, Los Blancos can rejoice in winning the transfer battle, and it remains to be seen how long it takes before JJ Gabriel is announced as a Real Madrid player.

item.title: The Shortlist: Yassir Zabiri should be on the Premier League elite's transfer radar as Racing Santander star rivals Raphinha, Kylian Mbappe & Lamine Yamal in La Liga scoring charts
item.description: Yasir Zabiri Shortlist - Getty/GOAL The Rennes loanee has hit the ground running in Spain, and could earn a big-money move to England if he can keep up his electrifying form "The way Racing Santander play is what convinced me to come here," Yassir Zabiri said after joining the La Liga outfit on loan from Rennes in August. "I also really like Spain, and I believe this is the right environment for me." Racing sporting director Chema Aragon also struck a confident chord at Zabiri's unveiling, adding: "He has the qualities we were looking for. He moves well into space, finishes chances effectively, is intelligent, and adapts quickly." They have both quickly been proven right. Before his debut, Zabiri set himself the target of scoring at least 10 goals for Racing. It's safe to say that he will smash that mark, having already found the net eight times through his first 11 appearances. The Moroccan forward is currently fourth in the race for the Pichichi - the top scorer award in La Liga - seven adrift of early leader Raphinha, four behind Kylian Mbappe and only two off Lamine Yamal. That is quite the feat for Zabiri, especially when you factor in that newly-promoted Racing are 16th in the table and don't have anywhere near the same depth as Barcelona or Real Madrid. Indeed, Zabiri's individual brilliance could be the difference between mid-table safety and a relegation battle for Racing, who secured their return to La Liga in May after a 14-year absence. Whatever happens, he is obviously destined for bigger things, with Aston Villa and Newcastle reportedly tracking the 21-year-old ahead of the January transfer window. Z abiri may even spark a bidding war among all of the Premier League's elite clubs: he's that good. What may seem like an overnight success story on the surface has actually been anything but; Zabiri has been knocked down repeatedly and is now being rewarded for getting back every time, driven by an unshakeable belief that his time would come. First steps Zabiri learned his trade in his homeland before earning his first shot in Europe as a teenager, but had to be patient for senior opportunities Zabiri started his footballing journey at KAC Marrakech before entering the prestigious Mohammed VI Football academy, which is also responsible for developing Morocco internationals such as Nayef Aguerd, Youssef En Nesyri and Azzedine Ounahi. "I'll be eternally grateful to the academy because it's better than many places in Europe," Zabiri told Diario AS . "Everything was at our disposal, whatever we needed, it was there." He graduated at the age of 18, and in January 2024, made his debut for the Union Touarga senior team. Across 11 appearances for the Botola Pro League club, Zabiri registered three goals, and caught the eye with his clever moment and positional sense in the final third. As a natural No.9 who is also capable of operating on either flank as an inside forward, Zabiri was soon being touted as one of the brightest talents in Moroccan

item.title: Barcelona midfield mainstay suffers hamstring injury in Aston Villa win; doubtful for Atletico Madrid clash
item.description: Barcelona midfield mainstay suffers hamstring injury in Aston Villa win; doubtful for Atletico Madrid clash Barcelona are monitoring Rodri’s fitness after the midfielder experienced discomfort in his right hamstring during 3-0 Champions League victory over Aston Villa . According to Mundo Deportivo , the 30-year-old asked to be substituted after feeling pain toward the end of the first half, prompting Hansi Flick and the club’s medical staff to leave him out of the second half. The incident comes at an important moment for Barcelona, who face Atletico Madrid in LaLiga on Sunday, November 8. Rodri’s availability will depend on the outcome of his medical assessment, with the Catalans reluctant to risk aggravating the problem. Rodri to undergo medical tests after Aston Villa substitution Rodri reportedly experienced discomfort in his right hamstring during the closing stages of the opening half against Aston Villa and reports state that he is doubful for weekend’s clash against Atletico. He managed to complete the first 45 minutes before informing Flick and the first-team doctors about the problem. Following their discussion at half-time, all parties agreed that continuing would be an unnecessary risk. Marc Bernal eventually replaced the midfielder, taking up the holding midfield position alongside Pedri. The academy graduate delivered a positive performance after the interval, helping Barcelona maintain their defensive structure and contain Aston Villa’s attacking threats. As per the outlet, Rodri is now scheduled to undergo medical tests on Wednesday during the club’s post-match recovery session. The assessment will establish whether he has sustained an injury and whether his participation against Atletico Madrid is in danger. Flick’s reliance on Rodri raises workload concerns The aforementioned incident also renews questions about Rodri’s playing time under Flick. Rodri was taken off at half-time. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Since signing from Barcelona and completing his registration, he has accumulated 945 minutes across 14 appearances this season, making him one of Barcelona’s most frequently used players. Despite his importance, however, his workload attracted attention during Saturday’s 6-1 victory over Alaves. Despite Barcelona establishing a 4-0 advantage before half-time, Flick substituted Pedri after 45 minutes and also gave Raphinha and Lamine Yamal periods of rest. Rodri, meanwhile, completed the entire match. Rodri’s potential absence would create a significant selection decision for Flick ahead of Sunday’s encounter, as Atletico are a demanding opponent and Barcelona would ideally want their regular midfield structure available. Bernal’s performance against Aston Villa provides a natural alternative in the holding midfield position, although replacing Rodri’s experience and positional influence would still be difficult.

item.title: Dark day for football, Joan Garcia’s show | Three takeaways from Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa
item.description: Dark day for football, Joan Garcia’s show | Three takeaways from Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa Barcelona returned to winning ways in the UEFA Champions League last night, racking up a commanding 3-0 win over Aston Villa, who were unbeaten in the competition up to that point. It only took seven minutes for the Catalans to take the lead against the Premier League side as Lamine Yamal latched onto an error by the Aston Villa defence and punished them brutally. The first half ended with the same scoreline, but Raphinha struck twice after the break to take the wind out of the visitors’ sails and engrave the result on stone. Barcelona now move to second place after four games, although Wednesday’s games will see some more clubs shift above them on the leaderboard. Barça Universal brings you three takeaways from Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa. A dark day for football The mood at the Spotify Camp Nou was not as jubilant as the venue usually boasts, as has been the mood in Spain in general over the past 24 hours. Camp Nou observed a minutes’ silence before kick-off. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) After all, the tragedy in Tenerife marked a dark day for football, which will go down in history as one of the most painful developments to ever unfold on a football field. The world of football has been shaken up by Jesus de Miguel’s tragic passing after getting on the receiving end of a reckless challenge in Tenerife’s recent game, and it is clear that the Barcelona dressing room is no exception. The mood last night, overall, was quite grim and the news undoubtedly had a big part to play. Ahead of kickoff, UEFA mandated a one-minute silence in honour of the departed soul and the Camp Nou obliged. Yet, celebrations were subdued against Aston Villa, and one would assume that the news weighed heavily on the players’ minds. Raphinha starred with a game-defining brace, but did not celebrate either goal with his usual energy as he looked disturbed and far from his usual fighting self. While Barcelona’s win against Aston Villa was massive, and helps the team get back on track in La Liga, some matters transcend football and De Miguel’s passing is one such tragic case. Rodri’s probable injury Rodri has quickly emerged as Hansi Flick’s most-trusted midfield options and the team find themselves relatively exposed at the back without his experience guarding the defence. Rodri might have picked up an injury. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) He started against Aston Villa last night and played a good shift in the first half. In 45 minutes, the former Ballon d’Or winner completed 92% of his 50 attempted passes. He also completed two long balls, nine progressive carries and made seven defensive actions against the Premier League side. He was, however, replaced at half-time quite surprisingly. The initial picture was that it was part of Flick’s usual rotation scheme, especially with the Atletico Madrid clash up ahead. Yet, it now appears that the player actually suffered an in

item.title: Fabrizio Romano drops major Carrick update after Roma win as INEOS identify preferred candidate
item.description: Fabrizio Romano drops major Carrick update after Roma win as INEOS identify preferred candidate Manchester United welcomed AS Roma on Tuesday night in hopes of putting an end to their nine-game winless run across all competitions. In the space of 17 minutes, Michael Carrick looked hopeless as he saw his side being completely outplayed by the visitors, who secured a two-goal lead through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen. The Italians came very close to making it three just before the break. However, in the second half, Carrick’s players produced an extraordinary performance to come back from two goals down and beat the Italian giants. That response may have a major impact on their head coach’s future. Manchester United will not pull the trigger After the Champions League clash, Fabrizio Romano took to his YouTube channel to provide an update on Michael Carrick ‘s situation at Manchester United. “This win means first of all one thing: Michael Carrick now continues his story as Manchester United coach. Michael Carrick will have more opportunities, including the next game,” claimed Romano. The Italian journalist insisted that beating Roma was “absolutely crucial” for Carrick and a defeat would have made it “really complicated” for the club legend to “survive”. “But for sure the indication is that now Carrick will get more opportunities, and this game with Roma will help to build,” added Romano. Man United last 10 matches (to 4 Nov 2026) Manchester United greatly admire Unai Emery United’s next challenge comes against Aston Villa, who are led by the brilliant Unai Emery. According to Romano, United “ideally consider” Emery a fantastic coach and “probably the right man to be the long-term” coach for the Red Devils. If the Spaniard manages to outclass Carrick at Old Trafford before the international break, he would certainly gain more supporters among the higher-ups at United. However, Romano suggested Villa have zero intention of letting Emery leave, especially in the middle of the season. The former Arsenal boss shares a great relationship with Villa’s board, who continue to strongly back him. Featured image by Dan Istitene via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier pulls off historic feat with goal-scoring barrage vs. Canucks
item.description: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier pulls off historic feat with goal-scoring barrage vs. Canucks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While the Anaheim Ducks have gotten off to an inconsistent start to the 2026-27 season just months after advancing to the Western Conference Semifinal in the spring, they’ve rattled off two straight wins and, on Tuesday night, exacted some revenge against a divisional opponent. The Ducks, who were beaten 6-5 in OT by the Vancouver Canucks last week after initially leading 5-2, improved to 7-7-1 with a 5-4 win over Vancouver at Rogers Arena. Helping to make it possible was forward Cutter Gauthier , who remained red-hot by scoring his second consecutive hat trick. And in doing so, Gauthier became the first player in Ducks team history to net hat tricks in consecutive games. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 🎩 HAT TRICK CUTTER GAUTHIER 🎩 Back-to-back hattys for Cut! The FIRST consecutive hat tricks in Ducks history! #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/fKUK6WAK5M — Anaheim Ducks (@AnaheimDucks) November 4, 2026 While the Ducks haven’t been around nearly as long as some other teams in the NHL, they’ve still boasted multiple high-profile names throughout their lineup over the years, including Paul Kariya, Teemu Selanne, Ryan Getzlaf, and Corey Perry, making Gauthier’s accomplishment no small feat. With the second straight hat trick effort, Gauthier is now up to 10 goals with five assists so far in 2026-27. Before the season, the Ducks re-signed Gauthier to a six-year, $81 million contract extension. “We are pleased to get Cutter signed to a long-term deal and have him in camp on time,” Ducks general manager Pat Verbeek said via NHL.com. “He’s a major part of our young core, a pure goal-scoring talent that will continue progressing into an elite NHL player.” “This is a very exciting day for my family and me,” Gauthier said. “I’m so pleased to be able to sign long-term with the Ducks and be part of what I believe is a great future.” So far in his NHL career, Gauthier has scored 71 goals with 58 assists in 173 games played. item.title: Bayern still in ‘contact’ to sign Man Utd player
item.description: Bayern still in ‘contact’ to sign Man Utd player Bayern Munich are still in contact with wantaway Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel to sign him in the January transfer window. The 16-year-old teenager has expressed his desire to leave Old Trafford, and while Man Utd have not officially terminated his registration, the general expectation is that he will leave at some point in the next year. La Liga giants, Barcelona and Real Madrid are reportedly interested in securing his services, but Bayern are also in the race to sign the prodigiously gifted youngster. JJ Gabriel future: Bayern still in contact (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) Christoph Freund has publicly shared his admiration for the youngster, and Bayern are committed to developing players for the future . Christian Falk explained the backdrop of JJ Gabriel’s situation here , and the Bild journalist has further exclusively told CFBayern Insider that the Bavarian giants are still in contact with the player’s camp over a potential move. Bayern are currently struggling with injury problems. Ismael Saibari has undergone surgery for ligament tear, while Serge Gnabry is out for the rest of the year. With Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz also struggling with fitness issues, Bayern could be forced to delve into the transfer market in January. Bayern, in any way, will have to sign a new left winger in the summer, and if they opt to go for a new attacker now, they should go for JJ Gabriel, rather than losing to Madrid or Barcelona in the summer window. Falk says that the move also helps Gabriel, as he can acclimatise for the rest of the season, while he can get playing time due to injuries to other players. Paris Saint-Germain have also been linked, but Bayern are amongst the three top clubs that are heavily interested in signing the youngster. JJ Gabriel: Man Utd career over? (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) The youngster has already requested to leave Old Trafford, although Man Utd have been attempting to resolve their differences with the teenager and his family for the past few weeks. Gabriel joined the Red Devils’ academy at the age of 11 and has proved himself to be one of the most exciting young attackers in world football. He scored 29 goals in 32 appearances for United’s Under-18s before joining the senior squad for pre-season, but has not made his debut. Gabriel’s representatives requested assurances over regular game time, but Man Utd have failed to guarantee that , and as a result, there are strong disagreements over his development pathway. In case, he moves abroad, the Red Devils could receive only a modest training compensation payment rather than a substantial transfer fee.

item.title: ‘He Didn’t Hesitate for Half a Second’ — Media Insider Recalls Joe Buck’s Immediate Response on Working Without Troy Aikman
item.description: NFL analyst Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. There has been a ton of speculation about a true resolution to the entire cycle around Troy Aikman and ESPN. Aikman, one of the premier analysts in the announcing booth, does not have a contract beyond Super Bowl LXI, but his partner in the booth, Joe Buck, has already signed a new deal, leading to some tension between the two. Media insider Jimmy Traina says he checked in on how Buck feels about potentially going about his business without the Dallas Cowboys legend alongside him. Jimmy Traina Recalls Joe Buck’s Surprising Answer About Working Without Troy Aikman Over the last few weeks, the story between Aikman, Buck, and ESPN has been among the biggest topics on virtually every Monday Night Football broadcast. After retiring from the NFL, Aikman quickly joined the broadcasting booth. Within a year, starting in 2002, he was working alongside Buck, a partnership that has continued to this day across Fox and ESPN. In 2022, the two came over to ESPN, taking up their current roles on MNF. But that partnership could be nearing an end, with this season shaping up to be their last year together in the booth. As a hypothetical, Traina says he asked Buck a while ago what it would be like to call Monday Night Football without Aikman. “When this story broke with Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, I immediately thought of that conversation with Joe Buck,” Traina admitted. “I said, ‘Could you imagine ever doing Monday Night Football or working with someone other than Troy?'” As he spoke to Underscore Media , he admitted his shock: “I remember in that moment being struck by the fact that not only did Joe say vehemently he could work with anyone and he doesn’t have to just work with Troy, but he didn’t hesitate for half a second.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Moreover, Traina added that he believes Buck already knew something was about to go down, and that was a possible admission or hint from his end about what the future held. Since the storyline has gained traction, there have been reports of a tense verbal altercation between the broadcasting partners. Per those reports, Aikman accused Buck of being the reason behind ESPN’s hesitation in offering him an extension. Buck, on the other hand, claimed he played no role in steering the network that way. As things stand, Aikman still doesn’t have a deal in place with ESPN, and with how tense things have gotten, it’s unclear if there is going to be a resolution, even with a Super Bowl on the horizon. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Nikola Jokic Admits What Went Wrong After Loss to Trail Blazers
item.description: The Denver Nuggets had a hard-fought battle against the hot Portland Trail Blazers, but it was a battle they came out of as the losers 118-110 . Denver came out incredibly hot in the first quarter, outscoring Portland 31-19, but one thing that the Trail Blazers have proven this season is that their offense is not one to be trifled with, and their offense surged right back. Portland outscored Denver handedly the next three quarters on the way to the win. The Trail Blazers held the advantage from the three point line and moved the ball better than the Nuggets did, but the biggest factor that let Portland break away was the rebounding difference between the two teams. Portland out-rebounded Denver 53-37 and held a particular advantage with offensive rebounds, 21-9. Denver Nuggets guard Jamal Murray (27) controls the ball as forward Aaron Gordon (32) screens against Portland Trail Blazers guard Jrue Holiday (5) in the fourth quarter at Ball Arena. Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Gap in Rebounding That difference in rebounding created gave Portland's already formidable offense an advantage that it didn't need and did just enough to keep them out of reach for Denver, despite a good scoring night from the Nuggets as well. Rebounding, or a lack thereof, has become somewhat of a recurring issue for the Nuggets. They're near the middle of the pack when it comes to team rebounds per game at 42.5 per game, but that will only continue to grow as an issue the longer that the Nuggets continue to stagnate in that area. Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic (15) reacts in the fourth quarter against the Portland Trail Blazers at Ball Arena. Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Star Nuggets center Nikola Jokic has acknowledged the issue, and he chalks up those struggles, particularly against the Trail Blazers, to an inability to box out their opponents, leading to an abundance of offensive boards that as further enhanced by how readily Portland was shooting three pointers. "They [Portland] shot 41 threes, so the ball's going to bounce everywhere," Jokic said (via Nuggets ). "If... you're boxing your guy out, that's going to help us a lot." Denver Nuggets guard Christian Braun (0) controls the ball as Portland Trail Blazers guard Jrue Holiday (5) defends against center Nikola Jokic (15) as center Donovan Clingan (23) looks on in the fourth quarter at Ball Arena. Isaiah J. Rebounding not only helps create more offensive opportunities for Denver, it takes away those same opportunities for their opponents, which would have helped greatly in avoiding their defeat. item.title: Four Nigerian-Americans win US midterm elections
item.description: Four Nigerian-Americans have won elective positions in the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, while the outcome of another candidate, Segun Adeyina, remained pending in Georgia as votes were being counted. Jawando. Photo: Wusa9 The winners are Will Jawando, Junior Ezeonu, Oye Owolewa and Carol Kazeem, who secured positions in local government and state legislatures across Maryland, Texas, Washington, DC, and Pennsylvania. In Maryland, Jawando, the Democratic candidate, won the race for Montgomery County executive, defeating Republican candidate Esther Wells. Results published by NBC Washington on Wednesday showed Jawando polling 237,383 votes, representing 78.15 per cent, against Wells’s 66,383 votes, or 21.85 per cent, with 72 per cent of the expected votes counted. READ ALSO; US Midterms: Democrats take control of US Congress as voters reject Trump’s Republicans Jawando, who previously served on the Montgomery County Council, is the son of a Nigerian father and an American mother. His Nigerian heritage and political career have featured in reports by The Baltimore Banner and The Washington Post. In Texas, 27-year-old Ezeonu secured a seat in the state House of Representatives for District 101. He had defeated incumbent Chris Turner in the Democratic primary and was the only candidate on the ballot for the November general election after no Republican entered the race. According to his campaign biography, Ezeonu was born in Onitsha, Anambra State, and moved to Texas at the age of two. He was elected to the Grand Prairie City Council in 2021 and later became the city’s youngest mayor pro tempore. Oye Owolewa. Photo: Instagram (@repoyedc) In Washington, DC, Owolewa, the Democratic candidate, won an at-large seat on the District of Columbia Council. Local publication, The 51st, reported that Owolewa secured 69 per cent of the vote, against 21 per cent recorded by independent candidate Elissa Silverman. Owolewa, a pharmacist and son of Nigerian immigrants from Kwara and Osun states, previously served as the District’s elected shadow representative. The position allows its holder to advocate for Washington, DC, statehood but does not confer voting rights in the US Congress. Meanwhile, Kazeem, also a Democrat, retained her seat in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, representing District 159. The result of Adeyina’s contest in Georgia had yet to be called as of Wednesday, with votes still being counted. item.title: Sabres Get Major Zach Benson Update After Missed Practice
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Zach Benson #6 of the Buffalo Sabres controls a rebound in front of Anton Forsberg #31, Quinton Byfield #55 and Brandt Clarke #92 of the Los Angeles Kings with Peyton Krebs #19 during the first period at Crypto.com Arena on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty The Buffalo Sabres got some worrisome news on Monday. In addition to Konsta Helenius being ruled out as week-to-week, Zach Benson missed practice. It wasn’t necessarily an expected absence, and so it raised worries about a potential injury absence for the dynamic winger. Buffalo was returning home from a West Coast trip, and the Sabres are due to host the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday. A Benson absence would make things a bit tougher against a Senators team that has played well in the early going this season. The Sabres got better news on Tuesday, though, and can likely enter Wednesday without feeling too intimidated about what’s going on with Benson. Zach Benson Update The Sabres look set to have Benson available on Wednesday. Head coach Lindy Ruff told reporters Tuesday that after the missed day of practice, Benson returned on Tuesday and looked ready to take part in Wednesday’s clash. It was actually an action-packed Ruff update, shared by Sabres reporter Carson Gates: Lindy Ruff said Zach Benson had a good day and will be available to play tomorrow Said Alex Lyon is “close to being ready.” Conor Timmins didn’t feel good yesterday, but felt much better today. Will be ready “fairly soon” and will be a “welcome addition” to the Sabres PK Kulich is close to returning and is still an option for tomorrow Also said Noah Östlund is a “coach’s dream” with how he plays at both ends of the ice Says he will wait to manage the goalie situation until Lyon is ready, which is “days away.” Said all three guys can help win them games, and having the extra guy is very valuable — Carson Gates (@Gatesy35) November 3, 2026 The potential return of Alex Lyon is another big one for Buffalo, and that appears to be coming sooner rather than later. Benson, though, is the immediate win in this situation for the Sabres. Zach Benson’s Impact During the 2026 playoffs, Benson proved himself to be one of those players that’s much more fun to have on your own team than on the other side. And even as he struggled to find his first goal this season, Benson’s line was outshooting opponents by a ton. He’s a clear game-changing player while on the ice, even in his own way. That’s why it’s so crucial to Buffalo that he’s out there. And after a brief scare, it looks like the Sabres will continue to be able to count on Benson going forward. item.title: Cole Palmer third fastest to 50 Premier League goals for Chelsea
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - AUGUST 24: Cole Palmer of Chelsea celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Fulham and Chelsea FC at Craven Cottage on August 24, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) | Chelsea FC via Getty Images Cole Palmer reached a bit of a milestone with his successful penalty against Manchester United over the weekend: it was his 50th goal for Chelsea in the Premier League. And yet it was only his 105th appearance in the Premier League for Chelsea! That’s good enough for third fastest all-time , behind both Jimmy-Floyd Hasselbaink (84 goals) and Diego Costa (85), but just ahead of Didier Drogba, who took one more at 106. Beating Drogba to this mark is especially impressive, though our legendary striker did get off to a slow start in his Chelsea career, and he’s more famous for his big goals on the biggest occasions (a habit that Cole’s also slowly developing ). Palmer’s the eighth player to reach 50 goals for us in the Premier League (Frank Lampard, Eden Hazard, Gianfranco Zola, and Eidur Gudjohnsen also got there, in addition to the three already mentioned), and he’s the 28th player to reach 50 goals in any domestic league competition in our history. Overall, he’s got 59 Chelsea goals in all competitions, good for 30th all-time already (incidentally, tied with both Costa and Nicolas Anelka). Here’s to the next 50!
